The sponsor must not downgrade the investigator's causality assessment; if it disagrees, both opinions are given in the SUSAR report.

f.title: Determine expectedness against the reference safety information valid at the time of the event
f.statement: Expectedness considers whether the event adds significant information on specificity, increased frequency or severity of a known serious reaction. The sponsor determines expectedness from the reference safety information (RSI), based on previously observed events with the active substance, not on expected pharmacological properties or disease-related events. The RSI is in the SmPC or the Investigator's Brochure; the cover letter states where it is located; in multinational trials the sponsor selects the SmPC most appropriate to subject safety. For SUSAR reporting, the RSI version valid when the SUSAR occurs applies. Expectedness information from the reporting investigator is taken into account.
